Every person the Old Testament gives a join for, on a
year scale. A box sits at its first dated year — birth
where the text gives it, accession for a king — and the
rail on the left says which year that is.
Only 87 of the 1232 people here can be dated at all.
Those boxes carry their years. Everyone else sits
between the nearest dated ancestor and descendant
on their line, in proportion to the generations
between; with no dated descendant, a generation …
Years are Ussher's, as the Authorized Version
printed them: creation 4004 BC, the Masoretic ages
in Genesis 5 and 11, Abram born when Terah was
130. The right-hand rail shows where the modern
The scale is not even, and says so. It opens out wherever the tree is dense — no
box may sit closer to its father than his box is tall — and closes up where nothing
is recorded. Read the spacing of the century marks on the rail to see where.
a life the text measures, birth to death
a reign — accession to end; overlaps are co-regencies
a person placed by one event the text ties him to
THE TEXT COUNTS THE YEARS · 4004 – 1706 BC
Genesis 5 and 11 give every man's age at his son's birth and at his death. Nothing here
rests on any source but the verses.
430 years in Egypt or 215; 480 to the Temple or 440 or the sum of Judges. Drawn on
Ussher's reading, but the ends are soft.
THE KINGS, YEAR BY YEAR · 1095 – 588 BC
Regnal years, summed. From about 850 BC the Assyrian eponym canon anchors them
to the calendar — the right-hand rail shows where the two counts part company.
Persian reigns are fixed by Babylonian astronomy; the biblical events float inside them.
From Jaddua to Joseph the genealogy is not recorded. Matthew's ten names and Luke's
eighteen cross the gap, and share none.
WHAT THIS SHEET WILL NOT DO
It will not settle the forks. The Septuagint's ages put creation some 1,400 years earlier;
Exodus 12:40 reads 430 years in Egypt or 215; 1 Kings 6:1 reads 480 or 440. The sheet
takes one reading of each and names it.
It will not bridge Jaddua to Joseph. The text does not, and Matthew's ten names across
those five centuries — fifty years a generation — are a pattern of fourteens, not a census.
It will not give Jesus a year. Ussher's 4 BC is AM 4000; Herod died in 4 BC; Luke's
